Agello's MemoryProbe (93122b647a) reads the footprint as task_vm_info.phys_footprint from task_info(TASK_VM_INFO) and the headroom from os_proc_available_memory(); DeviceProfile.current sets appMemoryLimitBytes to their sum when the available value is greater than 0, and to nil otherwise.

Agello's DeviceProfile.maxContextTokens (93122b647a) returns 32,768 when the app memory limit is at least 6,500,000,000 bytes and 16,384 when it is lower or unknown (nil), so an iPhone 17 Pro limit of 8,589,934,592 bytes gives 32,768 and 6,442,450,944 bytes gives 16,384.

In Agello at 93122b647a, DeviceProfile.maxContextTokens is read only by the KV-cache Stepper of AdvancedSettingsView (range 256...DeviceProfile.current.maxContextTokens(model:)) and by unit tests; with the 6 GiB (6,442,450,944-byte) reading an iPhone 17 Pro returns in the first seconds after launch, that stepper would end at 16,384 tokens instead of 32,768.

text: ML Drift's Metal backend (15fa9e2) creates its MTLBuffers with MTLResourceStorageModeShared and its standalone textures with MTLStorageModePrivate.

LiteRT's Metal buffer handler (362759838) writes host data into a packed Metal buffer with memcpy when the buffer is shared, and also for managed buffers with didModifyRange only under TARGET_OS_OSX; otherwise it uses a blit.

LiteRT-LM's AdvancedSettings::gpu_enable_metal_residency_set defaults to false, Swift's ExperimentalFlags.gpuEnableMetalResidencySet defaults to nil, and Agello at 93122b647a sets ExperimentalFlags.enableBenchmark and filterChannelContentFromKvCache but not gpuEnableMetalResidencySet, so with LiteRT's GpuBackendMetal (which attaches and requests its residency set only when the option is on) residency is not requested in Agello's configuration of the documented build.

Apple's feature set tables list residency sets for Apple6 and later with at most 32 residency sets per queue, and Apple's MTLResidencySet documentation (iOS 18.0 and later) says residency sets don't track hazards.

text: LiteRT-LM's C header documents litert_lm_engine_settings_set_gpu_enable_metal_residency_set as using MTLResidencySet on Apple platforms with the GPU backend to keep model weights and allocations resident, and as recorded but without effect elsewhere.

LiteRT-LM's SetCommonGpuOptions calls SetUseMetalArgumentBuffers(true) under __APPLE__ and LiteRT's Metal delegate turns the option off only when argumentBuffersSupport == MTLArgumentBuffersTier1; with Apple's tables putting tier 2 argument buffers at Apple6 and later, the documented build binds kernel arguments through argument buffers on every Apple6 or newer GPU, including every iPhone Agello supports.

text: Agello's scripts/device-harness.sh (93122b647a) passes AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU to the app under test by exporting TEST_RUNNER_AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU, the prefix xcodebuild strips when it sets the test runner's environment.

ML Drift (15fa9e2) lowercases AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU and matches it against the same name keys as device names ('apple a17 pro', 'apple m2', ...), so a value such as 'A17 Pro' matches no key, leaves AppleGpu::kUnknown and family Apple1, and our LiteRT (362759838) then reports a kGpuFamilyUnknown anomaly in GpuBackendMetal::GetInfo.

With AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU='Apple A17 Pro' on the iPhone 17 Pro, Agello's harness still records gpuAppleFamily 10 (Apple's supportsFamily) and the device's 8.590 GB limit, because the switch changes only ML Drift's AppleInfo, not the MTLDevice.

Simulator doesn't try to exactly simulate the GPU from the iOS, tvOS, or visionOS device you're simulating.

text: ML Drift (15fa9e2) sets MetalInfo::is_simulator when the original (not lowercased) Metal device name contains 'simulator', and GpuInfo::SupportsImageBuffer returns false for Metal when is_simulator is set; the family still comes from the name table, so a device name containing no known chip name gives Apple1.

The rule that Agello never runs in the simulator rests on our framework having no simulator slice (//agello:CLiteRTLM builds iOS device arm64 and macOS arm64 only) and on project policy; Google's shipped v0.18.0 framework has a simulator slice containing the Metal accelerator, and whether it runs Gemma 4 E4B in the simulator has not been tested.
